extracted.intended_audience: UK public authorities, bodies exercising public functions, legal practitioners and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory guidance in Section 149 of the Equality Act 2010 setting out the public sector equality duty: the obligations on public authorities (and those exercising public functions) to have 'due regard' to eliminating prohibited conduct, advancing equality of opportunity, and fostering good relations, with particular detail on duties regarding disabled persons and protected characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public authority duty to have due regard
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A public authority must, in the exercise of its functions, have due regard to the need to— (a) eliminate discrimination, harassment, victimisation and any other conduct that is prohibited by or under this Act; (b) advance equality of opportunity between persons who share a relevant protected characteristic and persons who do not share it; (c) foster good relations between persons who share a relevant protected characteristic and persons who do not share it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation applies when exercising any functions; 'have due regard' signals a proportional consideration of the three aims (eliminate discrimination; advance equality; foster good relations) during decision-making and policy implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons exercising public functions (non-public authorities) duty
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) A person who is not a public authority but who exercises public functions must, in the exercise of those functions, have due regard to the matters mentioned in subsection (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends the duty beyond formal public bodies to private or hybrid bodies when they perform public functions; such persons must apply the same 'due regard' consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: What 'advance equality of opportunity' involves (particular considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) Having due regard to the need to advance equality of opportunity between persons who share a relevant protected characteristic and persons who do not share it involves having due regard, in particular, to the need to— (a) remove or minimise disadvantages suffered by persons who share a relevant protected characteristic that are connected to that characteristic; (b) take steps to meet the needs of persons who share a relevant protected characteristic that are different from the needs of persons who do not share it; (c) encourage persons who share a relevant protected characteristic to participate in public life or in any other activity in which participation by such persons is disproportionately low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists concrete focal points when advancing equality: identifying and removing linked disadvantages, addressing differing needs, and taking positive steps to boost participation where underrepresentation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting needs of disabled persons (specific requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) The steps involved in meeting the needs of disabled persons that are different from the needs of persons who are not disabled include, in particular, steps to take account of disabled persons' disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that reasonable adjustments or steps should explicitly take account of disabilities; signals heightened or particularised consideration for disabled persons under the duty to advance equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: What 'foster good relations' involves (particular considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) Having due regard to the need to foster good relations between persons who share a relevant protected characteristic and persons who do not share it involves having due regard, in particular, to the need to— (a) tackle prejudice, and (b) promote understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming to foster good relations, public authorities should prioritise activities and policies that reduce prejudice and increase mutual understanding between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted differential treatment in pursuit of duties (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) Compliance with the duties in this section may involve treating some persons more favourably than others; but that is not to be taken as permitting conduct that would otherwise be prohibited by or under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that positive or preferential measures (e.g., positive action) can be lawful to meet the duty, but such measures must not contravene other prohibitions in the Act (they do not create a blanket exemption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant protected characteristics (enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: (7) The relevant protected characteristics are— age; disability; gender reassignment; pregnancy and maternity; race; religion or belief; sex; sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory list of characteristics that public authorities must consider under the duty; these are the categories referenced throughout the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'conduct that is prohibited' for the duty
rubrics_metrics.description: (8) A reference to conduct that is prohibited by or under this Act includes a reference to— (a) a breach of an equality clause or rule; (b) a breach of a non-discrimination rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the scope of 'prohibited conduct' includes breaches of equality clauses/rules and non-discrimination rules, tying the duty directly to other enforceable legal obligations within the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions (Schedule 18) apply
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts that specified statutory exceptions (in Schedule 18) can modify or limit the application of the duties; public authorities should consult Schedule 18 where relevant.
